title: Company Secretary Assistant
description:
Company Secretarial Assistant

We're working with a FTSE 250 organisation that is expanding its Company Secretarial team and is looking for a Company Secretarial Assistant. This is a brilliant opportunity to develop your technical knowledge, gain exposure to a diverse client portfolio, and grow your career within a fast-paced, ambitious business that's committed to excellence in governance.

Perks
- Salary- £40-50k depending on experience
- London City Office
- Performance-based bonus
- Generous employer pension contributions
- Private healthcare cover
- Health cash plan
- Life assurance
- Buy/sell annual leave scheme
- Structured development pathway with opportunities for progression

What You'll Be Doing

Key responsibilities include:
- Conduct thorough reviews of company secretarial work, including board minutes and resolutions, shareholder resolutions and statutory filings, ensuring accuracy, completeness and compliance with legal and regulatory requirements
- Monitor adherence to internal processes, standards and best practices, identifying any gaps or inconsistencies
- Ensure that all statutory filings comply with the Companies Act and other relevant laws and regulations
- Maintain oversight of electronic corporate records using Diligent Entities to ensure data integrity and regulatory compliance and undertake any statutory filings with the Registrar of Companies
- Work closely with team members to provide feedback on their work, identifying opportunities for improvement and ensuring high-quality service delivery
- Support the development of standardised templates, guidance notes and best practice frameworks to enhance efficiency and accuracy in corporate secretarial processes
- Contribute to the development and refinement of internal procedures, ensuring they align with evolving legal and regulatory requirements
- Provide coaching and training to team members on quality standards, governance requirements and best practices in company secretarial work
- Provide advice on corporate governance best practice and reviewing relevant documentation
- Support professional development by sharing insights and feedback to enhance technical knowledge and skill levels within the team
- Conduct periodic reviews and refresher sessions to reinforce key compliance and quality expectations
- Support the development of quality assurance reporting metrics to track performance and areas for improvement

About You

We're looking for an enthusiastic, proactive professional who is keen to grow within the company secretarial field.

You will ideally:
- Be CGI part or fully qualified (or other professional qualification if relevant experience can be demonstrated)
- Enjoy collaborating with peers and sharing knowledge
- Pro-actively request and act upon feedback received on the quality of work produced

Interested? Let's talk.

If you're ready to join a respected FTSE 250 company where you'll be supported to learn, grow and make a real impact, do reach out. This role won't be around for long, so don't delay - apply today!

title: Income Administrator
description:

Essential Requirements
- Previous experience in administration, finance or income management.
- Strong numerical skills and excellent attention to detail.
- Good communication and customer service skills.
- Confident using Microsoft Office, spreadsheets and database systems.
- Ability to manage competing priorities and meet deadlines.
- A professional, organised and proactive approach.
- Ability to work independently and contribute effectively within a busy team.

Desirable Experience

Experience within a housing association, local authority or social housing environment is highly desirable. Knowledge of rent accounts, income collection, arrears monitoring, housing management systems and welfare benefit-related rent queries would be an advantage.

What We Offer
- Competitive hourly rate, dependent on experience.
- An opportunity to gain further experience within the social housing sector.
- A supportive and professional working environment.
- The opportunity to contribute to an important housing management function.
- Potential to develop your skills and experience in income management.

Are you an experienced Construction Administrator or Project Administrator with a background in the building industry? Are you organised, proactive and confident coordinating multiple jobs in a busy construction environment?

We are recruiting for a Project and Planning Administrator to join a well-established, family-run building company based in Greenford, Middlesex. The business specialises in building refurbishments, renovations, reactive maintenance and emergency repair works.

Working within the Projects team, you will provide essential administrative and coordination support across a range of construction projects, insurance claims and building works. You will liaise with clients, contractors, tradespeople and colleagues to ensure jobs are organised efficiently, deadlines are monitored and customers receive a professional service throughout the process.

This is an excellent opportunity for an experienced construction administrator who enjoys working in a fast-paced environment and wants to join a small, supportive team.

Key Responsibilities
- Provide day-to-day administrative support to the construction Projects team.
- Coordinate and monitor ongoing building projects, insurance claims, refurbishments and reactive maintenance jobs.
- Manage team diaries, schedule appointments and arrange site visits for tradespeople and operatives.
- Book repairs and building works, ensuring appointments and schedules are maintained.
- Monitor job progress and proactively chase outstanding information, documentation and approvals.
- Handle incoming telephone calls, emails and customer enquiries professionally and efficiently.
- Liaise with clients, customers, contractors, tradespeople and internal colleagues to keep projects moving.
- Maintain accurate project records and update CRM systems and job management software.
- Monitor deadlines and ensure jobs are progressed in line with agreed service levels.
- Update project budgets, purchase orders and invoice payments.
- Prepare and issue invoices and customer payment links.
- Assist with data entry, filing, correspondence and general office administration.
- Process office-related invoices and staff expense claims.
- Support the Projects Manager with workload planning, reporting and day-to-day team coordination.
- Provide a professional and empathetic service to customers, particularly those dealing with insurance claims or urgent building repairs.

Essential Skills and Experience

To be considered for this position, you must have:
- A minimum of three years' experience in project administration, planning or coordination within the construction or building industry.
- Previous experience working for a construction contractor, building company, refurbishment business, property maintenance provider or similar construction-related organisation.
- Strong organisational skills, with the ability to coordinate multiple jobs and prioritise competing deadlines.
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including a confident and professional telephone manner.
- Strong numeracy skills and a high level of accuracy when handling budgets, purchase orders, invoices and project records.
- Good working knowledge of Microsoft Office 365, particularly Excel and Word.
- Experience using CRM systems, job management software or similar administrative applications.
- The ability to communicate effectively with clients, contractors, tradespeople and colleagues at all levels.
- A proactive approach to problem-solving, with the ability to use initiative and work independently.
- Good written English and the ability to produce clear, professional correspondence.
- The ability to work effectively within a small team in a busy, fast-paced environment.

Experience with insurance claims, reactive repairs, construction scheduling, contractor coordination or property reinstatement works would be particularly beneficial.

Location Requirement - Applicants must live within a maximum one-hour commute of Greenford, Middlesex.

This is a fully office-based position, Monday to Friday. Candidates must be able to commute to the Greenford office daily within the stated travel time.

Applications from candidates who live beyond a reasonable one-hour commute will not be considered.

Salary and Benefits
- £27,000 £33,000 per annum, depending on relevant experience.
- Permanent, full-time employment.
- Monday to Friday, 9:00am 5:00pm.
- One-hour lunch break.
- Pension scheme.
- Smart-casual dress code.

title: Project Administrator

- Supportive and collaborative working environment.

title: Finance Officer
description:
Job Title: Finance Officer

Location: Barnes, South-west London, SW13 9 QN

Salary: Competitive

Job Type: Full time, Permanent

About Harrodian School:

The Harrodian School is a prestigious, selective independent co-educational day school located on a stunning 25-acre riverside estate in Barnes, South West London. Founded in 1993 on the former site of the Harrods staff sports club, the school offers a seamless all-through education for nearly 1,040 pupils aged 4 to 18.

Candidates should check that they live within a commutable distance before applying for this role.

About the Role:

The purpose of the role is to support the Finance Director in the day-to-day operation of the Finance Department, ensuring accurate financial processing and the efficient running of finance functions.

Ideally the right candidate will have experience within a similar School finance position and be confident with Sage 200 and SIMS.

Responsibilities:

Purchase Ledger:
- Enter supplier invoices and expense claims onto SAGE 200.
- Ensure delivery notes are signed to confirm receipt of goods and that order numbers are quoted.
- Match delivery notes with supplier invoices and match supplier invoices to Purchase Orders; liaise with suppliers and internal departments regarding discrepancies.
- Reconcile invoices with supplier statements prior to payment.
- Assist with quarterly VAT reviews of the Purchase Ledger, ensuring the accurate identification of recoverable and non-recoverable VAT.
- Submit daily cheque listings to the bank.
- Support the implementation and ongoing development of the new Purchase Order system.

Sales Ledger:
- Maintain the Sales Ledger, including production of termly bills and additional charges.
- Manage Direct Debit collections, including monitoring successful and failed payments and following up with parents where required.
- Process and allocate fee receipts in Sage 200.
- Handle fee queries from parents, contacting staff and the Headteacher where necessary, resolving the issue and responding formally to parents.
- Maintain confidentiality and comply with GDPR requirements when handling financial and personal data.
- Control and manage the debtors list, including debt recovery and the application of interest charges.
- Regular reconciliation of the bank account.
- Process Government support schemes, including EHCP funding.
- Issue non-school-fee invoices as required.

Other Duties:
- Data entry using Excel, Sage 200 and other software packages, e.g. Scopay.
- Attend departmental meetings as required
- Contribute to the smooth running of the Accounts department
- Participate in staff training, regular staff meetings, INSET days and other professional activities.
- Undertake any additional duties reasonably requested by the line manager that fall within the scope of the role.
- Provide ad hoc finance support to the Finance Director as required.

Job descriptions are subject to regular review at the discretion of the School.

About you:

Skills - Essential:
- Attention to detail
- Financially numerate
- Organised and efficient
- Strong communication skills
- Excellent IT skills (Office, Excel, SIMs)
- Collaborative and flexible

Personal Qualities - Essential:
- Kind, patient and discreet
- Calm under pressure
- Professional and reliable
- Uses initiative and takes responsibility
- Reflective and willing to improve

Experience:
- School-based finance experience, including the billing of school fees, is essential.
- Experience of Sage 200 Professional and Scopay/Stripe is desirable.
- A finance or accounting qualification is desirable.
- Experience working in a fast-paced environment.

Please click the APPLY button to submit your CV.

Candidates with the experience or relevant job titles of; Finance Administrator, Invoicing, Accounts, Finance Assistant, Account Assistant, Accounts Administrator, Purchase Ledger, Sales Ledger, Financial Assistant, Accounts Administrator, Accounts Clerk, Finance Clerk, Accounts Payable, Accounts Receivable, Credit Control will be considered for this role.

title: Credit Controller
description:
We are looking for an analytical and financially astute Credit Controller to join an established finance team in a role that goes beyond traditional debt collection.

Alongside managing outstanding debt, you will take ownership of income forecasting, complex debt analysis and high-level financial reporting, providing key insights to senior stakeholders, including the CFO and CEO.

With millions of pounds passing through the ledger each month, accuracy and forward planning are critical. You will need to understand what income is expected, identify potential shortfalls and ensure the right actions are taken to keep cash flow on track.

Key responsibilities
- Reporting and analysis: Produce detailed reports on debt, ledger movements, cash collected, accruals and income performance for senior management.
- Income forecasting: Monitor expected income, identify risks and highlight potential shortfalls well in advance.
- Complex debt management: Investigate aged and historic debt, resolve payment issues and develop solutions to secure outstanding income.
- Ledger oversight: Analyse variances, investigate discrepancies and ensure financial information is accurate.
- Business partnering: Lead financial review meetings with Heads of Service, discussing income performance, outstanding debt and agreed actions.
- Stakeholder engagement: Work closely with senior management, operational teams and finance colleagues to improve collection and financial visibility.
- Team support: Collaborate with the wider income team, balancing effective delegation with a hands-on approach.

About you

This role would suit someone looking to move beyond conventional credit control into a more analytical and commercially focused finance position.

You will bring:
- Experience in credit control, income management, debt analysis or a related finance role.
- Strong analytical skills and experience producing meaningful financial reports.
- An understanding of forecasting, cash flow, accruals and ledger management.
- The confidence to investigate complex debt, solve problems and take ownership.
- Strong communication skills and the ability to engage with senior stakeholders and operational teams.

Unit 4 experience would be beneficial but is not essential. Professional qualifications and sector experience are also not required; financial understanding, analytical ability and a proactive approach are the priorities.

The opportunity

This is an opportunity to develop beyond traditional credit control, gaining exposure to senior-level reporting, forecasting and business partnering within a supportive, established team.

For someone who enjoys working with financial data, solving complex problems and influencing decisions across the organisation, this role offers a strong platform for future progression into more senior finance responsibilities.

Working with bands, labels, distributors and musicians, the business looks after the finances behind the music. From day-to-day bookkeeping to monthly accounts and artist budgets, the team understands the industry and helps clients stay on top of their finances.

Working closely with the Finance Manager, you'll start with transactional accounting, gaining hands-on experience across accounts payable (AP), accounts receivable (AR) and reconciliations.

- Supporting accounts payable, processing supplier invoices and maintaining the purchase ledger.

As your knowledge and confidence develop, you'll get involved in month-end processes and monthly management accounts, progressing towards wider accounts preparation responsibilities. It's an opportunity to build strong foundations while working towards becoming an Assistant Accountant.

The candidate

You've started building your accounting knowledge. Now you're looking for somewhere to take it further, with people who will invest time in helping you grow.

You'll bring:
- A minimum of a years' experience in accounting or finance.
- A love for music.
- A foundation in double-entry bookkeeping, with an understanding of AP and AR.
- Confidence using Excel, including lookups and pivot tables.
- An eye for detail and the curiosity to work out why something doesn't reconcile.
- Good organisation, helping you stay on top of deadlines across different client accounts.
- Clear communication skills and a willingness to ask questions as you learn.

Bring your accounting foundations and the ambition to build on them, and you'll find a welcoming team ready to support your next step. With clients whose music might already be on your playlist, there's plenty to feel excited about.

Responsibilities:
Accounts Admin
- Collect supplier invoices and utility bills as they arrive by email and post. Download bills from supplier portals.
- Check each invoice against the order, contract or agreement. Send queries to whoever placed the order.
- Rename and file every invoice using the company's expense codes, by company and property.
- Prepare the weekly payment run for approval. Approved payments are made by James or Kate; the administrator does not authorise payments.
- Load payroll and PAYE payments from the figures the bookkeeper provides.
- Send the week's invoices to the bookkeeper on a set day and keep the reference copy filed.
- Keep the bank account and supplier details list up to date and confirm any change of supplier bank details by phone before it is used.
- Act as the bookkeeper's day-to-day contact for missing invoices, receipts and queries.
- Help set up and apply the new cost codes, so every cost is allocated to a property and a company.
- Gather the information needed for VAT returns, year-end accounts and confirmation statements, to the deadlines in the calendar.

Combined Calendar
Set up and run one calendar for the whole business, with reminders far enough ahead to act on:
- Accounts: VAT returns, annual accounts, confirmation statements and payroll dates, each with a preparation window before it.
- Property: rent due dates, rent reviews, lease breaks and expiries, and tenancy renewals.
- Compliance: gas safety, electrical, fire risk, EPC and other certificates, licences and inspections.
- Insurance: renewal dates.
- People: HR dates such as probation reviews and annual reviews.

Insurance Admin
- Keep the insurance schedule up to date: policies, renewal dates, premiums and documents.
- Be the brokers' day-to-day contact for documents, changes and renewals.
- Tell the brokers in writing about changes such as vacant units, changes of use and building works, as directed.
- Keep the claims file in order.
- Review policy documents and make sure their terms and conditions are kept to, for example inspections of vacant units, heating and water rules, tenant referencing and electrical safety reports. Diarise each condition and flag anything not being met.

Office, Post and Records
- Clear the backlog of paper records in the office: sort, scan where useful, file, and send to storage.
- Set up and keep a retention and destruction schedule for stored records, on the accountant's advice.
- Keep the office running: supplies, equipment, deliveries and visitors.
- Help with the office move in May 2027.

Company and Legal Administration
- Keep company records up to date for the four companies and prepare Companies House filings for approval.
- Keep registers of leases, tenancies, licences and key documents, and know where the originals are.

HR Admin
- Keep staff files: contracts, right-to-work checks, holiday and absence records.
- Diarise probation and annual reviews, and help prepare them.
- Help with recruitment admin: adverts, CVs, interview scheduling and onboarding.
- Keep HR policies filed and up to date, with the HR adviser.

IT & Systems
- Be the day-to-day contact for the IT provider: new users, laptops, access and faults.
- Help move files into the new shared document system and keep its folders tidy.

Supporting the team
- Support Associate Director with diary management, meeting notes, trackers and document preparation.
- Support the Property Manager, with document chasing, filing and tenancy paperwork. Keep the property management software, Konnexions, fully up to date and well managed: tenants, leases, rents, deposits, certificates, contacts and documents. The team needs all the information there to be accurate and current, because they rely on it to manage the portfolio.
- Work with the Liverpool team on shared admin tasks.

Skills and Experience Required:
- Minimum 5 years' experience in office or accounts administration within property
- Be confident with Xero and Excel
- Experience with property management software
- Excellent accuracy and attention to detail
- AAT Level 2 or equivalent bookkeeping knowledge

We are seeking an Analytics Officer to support by identifying why delays, duplication and process issues occur, and helping teams design simpler, more effective ways of working. This Analytics Officer position is suited to someone with strong business analysis capability, rather than purely technical data analysis experience. The successful Analytics Officer will work closely with colleagues to review current processes, establish credible baselines and support practical service improvement.

Day to day of the role
- Work with colleagues to understand current processes and uncover the root causes of delays, duplication and inefficiencies.
- Map end-to-end processes, including hand-offs, dependencies, local variation, rework and bottlenecks.
- Analyse workload, activity, timing, volumes and available resource to build a clear demand and capacity baseline.
- Identify gaps or limitations in available data and use sound judgement to present credible findings.
- Facilitate structured workshops with managers, team leaders and colleagues to gather insight and challenge assumptions constructively.
- Use spreadsheets and analytical tools to present performance, variation, demand and capacity information clearly.
- Help design improved ways of working that consider people, controls, systems and operational workload.
- Define measures, baselines, intended benefits, review points and data sources before implementation begins.
- Produce clear written outputs, including findings summaries, process maps, action logs, decision papers and implementation materials.

Required Skills & Qualifications
- Proven experience in business analysis, process improvement or service improvement roles.
- Strong process discovery and process mapping skills across multiple business areas.
- Ability to carry out demand and capacity analysis using incomplete or imperfect data sets.

description:

The Stroke Association is the only charity in the UK providing lifelong support for all stroke survivors and their families. This support includes one-to-one and group support, funding vital scientific research into stroke prevention, acute treatment, recovery and long-term care, and campaigning to secure the best care for everyone affected by stroke.

We re here for stroke survivors and their loved ones, from the moment they enter the new and frightening post-stroke world, supporting them every step of the way as they find their strength and their way back to life.

We are working to improve the representation of this lived experience at all levels within the Stroke Association and we are eager to recruit applicants from a variety of communities and backgrounds. We are keen to receive applications from people affected by stroke, people of colour, members of LGBT+ communities, and disabled people because these identities and experiences are underrepresented and would add enormous value to how we work.

We are a Disability Confident employer, and we are making great progress focusing on flexible working, reasonable adjustments and access to work. If you have questions, or access needs, we re happy to discuss any support and adjustments we can make throughout the recruitment process so that you re able to contribute your best in a way that meets your needs.

- 30,000 annual salary
- Fully remote working
- Head office based in Hounslow

title: Accounts Assistant
description:
Robert Half Finance & Accounting are partnering with a leading Public Sector Business in London to recruit an immediate, Interim Accounts Assistant for 3 months.

Role:

Our client is looking for an immediate interim Accounts Assistant to assist them for 3 months. You will be responsible for following duties:
- Assist the Head of Finance with the preparation of monthly management accounts up to trial balance, ensuring all entries are accurate, complete and processed within agreed deadlines.
- Assist the Head of Finance with the monthly reconciliation of all balance sheet accounts (including, accruals, prepayments, fixed assets, investments, AIF, lottery, contributions), post all relevant journals and ensuring any variances are investigated and resolved promptly.
- Assist the Head of Finance to perform monthly bank reconciliations across all accounts, ensuring all postings and allocations - both payments and receipts - are accurately recorded and fully reconciled.
- Assist the Head of Finance with the monthly reconciliation of credit and debit cards on a monthly basis, reviewing all data entered by the Finance Administrator to ensure accuracy and completeness.
- Work with the Head of Finance to carry out monthly period close for all ledgers in a timely and controlled manner, ensuring integrity of the financial records ahead of reporting.
- Assist the Head of Finance in preparing and submitting quarterly VAT Returns, ensuring accuracy and compliance with HMRC requirements.
- Regularly review modules within accounts software to ensure continuous and accurate flow of transactions, checking nominal codes and accounting periods for correctness.
- Work with the Head of Finance to process invoices when needed for head office and regional offices alongside the Finance Administrator, ensuring all invoices are coded correctly.
- Maintain a clean and well-managed creditors ledger at all times, ensuring all balances are clearly explained and any anomalies are accompanied by a documented action plan developed in liaison with Finance Administrator.
- Review invoices and payments processed by the Finance Administrator on a regular basis, ensuring transactions are accurate, appropriately coded and processed in a timely manner.
- Monitor cash position to advise the Head of Finance on whether the bank is sufficiently funded ahead of all proposed payment runs.
- Assist the Head of Finance in the accurate production and processing of monthly payroll and expenses in accordance with agreed timelines.
- Assist the Head of Finance to process payroll changes, liabilities invoices and payments, ensuring all associated entries are posted correctly and relevant parties are notified by email in a timely manner.
- Provide support during the annual budget exercise, assisting the Head of Finance with data gathering, analysis and preparation of relevant schedules.
- Assist during annual audit exercise, preparing reconciliations, schedules and supporting documentation as required by external auditors.
- Actively monitor accounts inbox, ensuring all incoming correspondence, invoices and queries are acknowledged and actioned promptly.
- Provide support to Finance Administrator as required, offering guidance and assistance to ensure smooth day-to-day running of finance function.

Profile:

The successful interim Accounts Assistant will have 2+ years experience.
You must be immediate or 1 weeks notice to be considered for this role.

This role is paying between £17-£20p/h + Holiday (DOE)

At Fujitec UK, we're in the business of keeping people moving. As part of an international lift and escalator business, we combine global expertise with a close-knit UK team that takes pride in what it does.

We're looking for an organised, upbeat and detail-focused Accounts Payable Administrator to join our Finance team for six months. We're introducing new finance systems and using this period to establish our longer-term needs. While that work progresses, you'll help keep our day-to-day finance operations running smoothly.

What you'll be doing
- Processing supplier invoices accurately and promptly, including matching them to purchase orders.
- Reconciling supplier statements, investigating discrepancies and keeping the purchase ledger up to date.
- Preparing information for supplier payment runs and supporting month-end activities.
- Responding to supplier queries and building positive relationships with colleagues across Finance, Purchasing and Operations.
- Allocating costs correctly to departments, contracts and projects, and maintaining reliable financial records.
- Helping the team maintain strong controls and efficient processes during the finance systems transition.

What you'll bring
- Practical experience in accounts payable, purchase ledger or a similar finance administration role.
- Confidence using accounting systems, Microsoft Excel and everyday office applications.
- Excellent attention to detail, numerical accuracy and organisational skills.
- A proactive approach to solving problems and managing competing priorities.
- A friendly, collaborative attitude and the ability to get up to speed quickly.

Experience in engineering, construction or a service-based business would be helpful, but it isn't essential. An AAT qualification is welcome, not required.

Why Fujitec?

You'll join a collaborative UK team within an established international business. Expect variety, plenty of people to work with and the satisfaction of making a practical difference at an exciting time of change. We value people who take ownership, support their colleagues and bring energy to the working day.

The details
- Location: Dartford, Kent
- Contract: six months, fixed term
- Salary: £28,000-£32,000 per annum, pro rata, depending on experience
- Working hours and start date: Monday to Friday 8.30am to 5pm with a 4.30pm finish on Fridays

Ready to get involved?

If you know your way around a purchase ledger, enjoy working with people and like getting things done, we'd love to hear from you. Apply today and help keep Fujitec moving!

Programme & Student Placements Administrator

Full time (35 hours) Fixed term for one year

Hybrid after completing probation

Salary: £26,590.00 per annum

Looking to broaden your experience in Higher Education?

We are looking for an organised and proactive administrator to join our Academic Affairs team. The role will predominantly support Programme Administration, including the day-to-day delivery of our academic programmes and student placements. You will also provide flexible administrative support across Academic Affairs, giving you the opportunity to gain experience across areas such as Quality, Student Records and Data, Timetabling and Student Life.

This makes the role a great opportunity for someone who already has experience working in education and wants to develop a broader understanding of Higher Education administration and the full student lifecycle.

You will work with Programme Directors, academic staff, students and colleagues across professional services, as well as supporting department managers and Heads of Service.

What you will be doing?

You will provide accurate and reliable administrative support across a range of activities including:
- programme and student administration
- assessment processes and Assessment Boards
- student records and regulatory processes
- student placements and associated documentation
- programme documentation and academic processes
- responding to routine queries from students and staff

Is this you?

Ideally, you'll have Higher Education experience, but we are also interested in applicants with relevant administrative experience from Further Education or another educational environment with comparable administrative processes.

More importantly, we're looking for someone who:
- is adaptable and flexible, and comfortable moving between different areas of work
- is proactive and able to progress tasks without needing everything prompted
- has excellent attention to detail, particularly when working with student data and official records
- is comfortable using a range of IT systems, with a basic working knowledge of Microsoft Excel being an advantage
- communicates clearly and professionally with students, colleagues and stakeholders
- can organise a varied workload, manage competing priorities and support colleagues where needed
- knows when they can resolve something themselves and when something needs to be escalated.

Why join us?

This isn't a role where you'll spend the whole year doing one narrow area of administration.

You'll build experience across Programme Administration while also getting exposure to different parts of Academic Affairs. You'll see how different teams contribute to the student journey, from programme and enrolment activity through assessment, records, quality and student support, giving you a much broader view of how Higher Education administration works.

For someone looking to take the next step in an HE administration career or make the move into HE from another relevant education setting, it's an opportunity to build practical experience across several areas within one role

title: Credit Controller
description:
Job Title: Credit Controller

Location: Sutton, SM3

Salary: Up to £40 K per year

Job type: Full Time - Permanent. 42.5 hours per week. Monday to Friday, 8am till 5.30pm.

We're looking for a proactive, resilient and innovative Credit Controller to join our Finance Team located at our Head Office in Sutton, SM3.

Our Creditor Controller will play a key part in the Business's income processing activity.

What you'll do:
- Reduce debt by collecting payments on time and within agreed payment terms and credit limits, using email, telephone and written follow-up.
- Ensure cash received is allocated to the correct accounts, and investigate, analyse and follow up on any underpayments or overpayments with the relevant team.
- Regularly reconcile accounts to ensure payments have been allocated correctly.
- Build and maintain effective relationships with key customers and internal stakeholders.
- Arrange and attend internal and external liaison meetings as needed to reduce debt risk and address barriers to payment.
- Review overdue historical debt and prepare reports identifying amounts that may qualify for write-off under the Bad Debt provision.
- Follow the escalation process for contested or non-recoverable debts after all recovery options have been explored, and present findings to the Finance Income Manager at scheduled debtor balance review meetings.
- Analyse Sales Ledger variances, identify potential issues, and agree action plans with our FD.

This is not an exhaustive list of all the duties and responsibilities that may be required from time to time and is subject to change in accordance with the needs of AAP.

About you:
- Enjoys social interaction and the company of others, joining local activities to encourage service-user involvement.
- Approachable and open behaviour
- Prefers working as part of a group or team
- Is calm and resilient, and does not allow emotion to affect judgement
- Has a practical and logical approach and is naturally well organised
- Thrives on change and enjoys dynamic, diverse environments
- Is confident and has strong self-esteem

What you'll bring:

Essential:
- At least two years' experience in a Credit Controller role
- Commercial exposure to the Income function
- Excellent time management skills, with the ability to manage own workload and meet agreed deadlines
- Excellent attention to detail
- Ability to work effectively under pressure
- Good IT and communication skills

Making you feel at home here means helping you thrive in every way. That's why we offer a wide range of benefits,

Our benefits include:
- Annual leave 23 days per annum plus all bank holidays
- A company pension
- Cycle to work scheme

All applicants must be legally eligible to work in the UK by the start of employment.

About us:

Advanced Access Platforms Ltd is a one of the countries largest privately owned plant hire company based in Sutton, Surrey, covering the south of the country specializing in powered access solutions. We are dedicated to providing exceptional customer service and cater to a diverse clientele, from large building contractors to small trades.

Candidates with relevant experience or job titles including; Credit Controller, Accounts Receivable Controller, Sales Ledger Controller, Credit Control Officer, Credit Control Administrator, Accounts Receivable Officer, Credit Management Officer, Credit Control Specialist, Debt Recovery Officer, Debt Collection Officer, Credit and Collections Analyst, Sales Ledger Administrator, Finance Credit Controller, Credit Control Executive, Accounts Receivable Assistant, may also be considered for this role.

Our reception team plays an essential role in ensuring the smooth and efficient running of the practice. As the first point of contact for many patients, you will help deliver a positive patient experience while providing essential administrative support to our clinical and management teams. We are looking for someone who is approachable, reliable, confident in communicating with patients and colleagues, and able to work effectively in a busy healthcare environment To cover reception desk, telephones and main reception duties in keeping with the Practice Protocol in a prompt and courteous manner giving your name as a first point of contact. To always be polite and courteous to patients presenting a positive image of the surgery and always maintaining patient confidentiality Take and redirect messages both accurately and in a timely manner. To liaise and answer questions from patients and all members of the Health Authority. supervise and assist, when necessary, any administrative staff or students in work placement. To make tea and coffee as necessary. To book and or email interpreters as and when required. To arrange appointments and send out recall letters for your allocated Chronic Disease Quality Marker Clinics. Adherence and assistance with the co-ordination of office rotas to ensure sufficient cover during breaks, annual leave and sick leave. To facilitate changeover between morning and afternoon shifts. To be flexible in the workplace in terms of hours worked and as and when the need arises. Attendance at practice and reception meetings, contributing to discussions on matters of practice policy affecting patients and staff. Open premises at the start of the day when first arrives, deactivate alarms and make all necessary arrangements to receive patients. Assist in the closing and securing of the building at the end of the working day Please see the attached job description, which sets out the main duties and responsibilities of the role in more detail and provides a fuller overview of what the position involves.

title: Receptionist
description: We are looking to appoint a motivated, reliable and hard working Receptionist. We have a part time position available, with the scope for full time. Previous Receptionist experience would be desirable. The first point of contact for patients and external services, face to face, on the phone and via email. To provide administrative support to the Practice Manager, GPs and health professionals including word processing, liaising with hospital administration teams and general clerical duties. Previous Receptionist experience would be desirable, as well as experience using EMIS and Docman. Torridon Road Medical Practice JOB DESCRIPTION JOB TITLE: RECEPTIONIST REPORTS TO: PRACTICE MANAGER (under the supervision of the Reception Supervisor) HOURS: 30 hours per week Job Summary: Receive, assist and direct patients in accessing the appropriate service or healthcare professional in a courteous, efficient and effective way. Provide general assistance to the Practice team and project a positive and friendly image to patients and other visitors, either in person or via the telephone. Job Responsibilities: Administration To have a thorough knowledge of all Practice procedures. To work in accordance of written protocols Pulling/filing notes for surgeries and update as necessary Incoming paperwork (e.g., post, requests for prescriptions, photocopying, faxes) Filing post in medical records Fax and photocopy as requested Outgoing paperwork (referrals, business letters, claims, forms, repeat prescriptions Reception Handing completed repeat prescriptions to patient and checking names and address. Be able to cover all reception position as necessary Contact with patients, appointments, greeting patients on arrival, directing as appropriate, dealing with visitors, informing patients of late running surgeries, registering new patients, explaining services Appointments Process appointment requests from patients by telephone and in person. Deal with visits requests Computer Registrations of new patients computer data entry and medical records. Process patients change of address computer data and medical records (have knowledge of Practice area. Process repeat prescription request in accordance with Practice guidelines. Telephone Have working knowledge of telephone, during and after hours. Cover for telephonist when necessary Other Tasks Clear rooms after surgeries Ensure building security have thorough knowledge of doors/windows/alarm. Make coffee for doctors Any other tasks allocated by managers organise catering for meetings handle cash safely and efficiently and maintain records Confidentiality: In the course of seeking treatment, patients entrust us with, or allow us to gather, sensitive information in relation to their health and other matters. They do so in confidence and have the right to expect that staff will respect their privacy and act appropriately In the performance of the duties outlined in this Job Description, the post-holder may have access to confidential information relating to patients and their carers, Practice staff and other healthcare workers. They may also have access to information relating to the Practice as a business organisation. All such information from any source is to be regarded as strictly confidential Information relating to patients, carers, colleagues, other healthcare workers or the business of the Practice may only be divulged to authorised persons in accordance with the Practice policies and procedures relating to confidentiality and the protection of personal and sensitive data Health & Safety: The post-holder will assist in promoting and maintaining their own and others health, safety and security as defined in the Practice Health & Safety Policy, to include: Using personal security systems within the workplace according to Practice guidelines Identifying the risks involved in work activities and undertaking such activities in a way that manages those risks Making effective use of training to update knowledge and skills Using appropriate infection control procedures, maintaining work areas in a tidy and safe way and free from hazards Reporting potential risks identified Equality and Diversity: The post-holder will support the equality, diversity and rights of patients, carers and colleagues, to include: Acting in a way that recognises the importance of peoples rights, interpreting them in a way that is consistent with Practice procedures and policies, and current legislation Respecting the privacy, dignity, needs and beliefs of patients, carers and colleagues Behaving in a manner which is welcoming to and of the individual, is non-judgmental and respects their circumstances, feelings priorities and rights. Personal/Professional Development: The post-holder will participate in any training programme implemented by the Practice as part of this employment, such training to include: Participation in an annual individual performance review, including taking responsibility for maintaining a record of own personal and/or professional development Taking responsibility for own development, learning and performance and demonstrating skills and activities to others who are undertaking similar work Quality: The post-holder will strive to maintain quality within the Practice, and will: Alert other team members to issues of quality and risk Assess own performance and take accountability for own actions, either directly or under supervision Contribute to the effectiveness of the team by reflecting on own and team activities and making suggestions on ways to improve and enhance the teams performance Work effectively with individuals in other agencies to meet patients needs Effectively manage own time, workload and resources Communication: The post-holder should recognize the importance of effective communication within the team and will strive to: Communicate effectively with other team members Communicate effectively with patients and carers Recognise peoples needs for alternative methods of communication and respond accordingly Contribution to the Implementation of Services: The post-holder will: Apply Practice policies, standards and guidance Discuss with other members of the team how the policies, standards and guidelines will affect own work Participate in audit where appropriate

title: Receptionist/Admin
description: We have 1 full time and 1 part time vacancy at Beam Park Medical Practice . Beam Park Medical Practice(BPMP)is looking to recruit an Full time and part time candidate Receptionist/ administrator to join our team. You will have good people skills to deliver patient services in an efficient and professional manner. You will also need to possess a high level of organisational skills, have excellent communication skills with a good team spirit. A high level of quality patient care is an integral part of this role. You will need to have the ability to be self motivated and be confident on using your own initiative within the limits of the role. If you are someone who is able to work well under pressure and maintain high quality service delivery, we would like to hear from you. Main duties of the job Handle incoming patient calls, respond to patient queries, and assist with appointment bookings. The primary function of the role is to deliver patient services in an efficient and professional manner Be welcoming, friendly and helpful to patients and visitors Working with the team, the front and back office team. To assist with the smooth running of the practice. To ensure that both front of house and administrative targets are met and maintained. Undertaking administrative tasks Liaising with healthcare professionals when necessary. Initiating contact with and responding to, requests from patients, team members and external agencies Helping new patients get settled into the practice by walking them through the process of officially joining the GP Open/close the practice at the beginning and end of each day and follow the opening and closing procedures Booking, cancelling, amending patients appointments using EMIS web clinical software To answer the telephone promptly and deal with enquiries in a helpful and courteous manner, being aware of the need to maintain confidentiality at all times regarding patients and staff. Manning the practices email inbox when needed To maintain a good rapport/relationship between internal and external patients of the Practice at all times. To have an overview of the demands and workflow of the Practice during the working day. Ensure the waiting area/reception front desk is kept tidy and keep forms and patient information stocked up where possible. Arranging appointments for patients reviews as part of QOF/PCN management Register new patients living within our catchment area Dealing with internal and external post To reach practice targets by asking patients to complete the patient friends and family surveys on a daily basis. Patient engagement proactively inform patients of benefits for signing up to the online services where patients can book appointments, order repeat prescription and view their medical record. Effectively signpost patients to services appropriate to their needs Scanning and action the clinical correspondence as per GP instructions into the patients medical records To be flexible to cover shifts in the event of staff holidays and sickness at short notice.

title: Receptionist / Administrator [PART TIME]
description: We are seeking a friendly and organised Receptionist / Administrator to join our team on a part time basis . We are looking for someone to work between 15 - 20 hours per week, over the course of the week. The timings and exact days will be discussed during the interview process. We can be flexible, within reason. The hours will be a mixture of morning shifts, starting at 8am and evening shifts finishing at 6:30pm, including the occasional Saturday shifts once the candidate is fully trained. We would ideally like the candidate to have experience working with the clinical system, SystmOne however this is not essential. We also use PATCHS and AccuRx so experience with this would be great. It is essential that you have experience of working with the public, customer service or patient facing type role. Full training will be provided either way. Experience of working within a GP practice is not essential. The practice is open Monday - Friday 08:00 - 18:30 & Saturday's 09:00 - 12:00. Provide a friendly and efficient first point of contact for patients and visitors, handling enquiries in person and by telephone and directing patients to the appropriate clinician or service. Manage appointment bookings and the flow of patients, record relevant information, and explain practice arrangements and registration requirements. Process new patient registrations, repeat prescription requests and patient correspondence; update records and scan documents into the clinical system. Use the appointment and telephone systems, take messages and ensure calls are routed appropriately. Keep reception and waiting areas tidy, maintain strict confidentiality, follow practice procedures, and support colleagues with cover and other delegated administrative duties. Ensure an effective, efficient and responsive reception service is provided to patients and all other visitors to the practice, including monitoring flow of patients into consulting and treatment rooms Deal with general enquiries, both over the telephone and in person, in a courteous manner and explain procedures where necessary. Take and disseminate messages when required. To deal with difficult patients, in reception and on the phone, in a calm manner and seek management support as and when required. Receive, assist and direct patients in accessing the appropriate service or healthcare professional in a courteous, efficient and effective way. Explain practice arrangements and formal requirements to new patients and those seeking temporary cover. Ensure necessary procedures are completed. Produce repeat prescriptions according to practice procedures and ensure timely distribution of completed prescriptions. Advice patients of relevant charges for private services, accept payment and issue receipts for the same. Ensure reception and waiting areas are kept neat and tidy. Receive and accurately record requests for home visits, assessing urgency in accordance with the Practice protocol. Re-stock practice rooms and re-order as appropriate. Participate in proactive forward planning identifying and implanting improvements within and beyond key result areas. To deal with complaints from the patients and other visitors and deal with them in line with the practice policy and procedures. Assist with the production of general letters and reports, medical insurance reports, letters and referrals for professional staff as and when required. Management of Appointment Systems and medical records Ensure total familiarity with appointment systems through training and self-assessment on System One. To signpost patients to the most appropriate healthcare professional i.e. ANT, HCA, Nurse and/or GPS. Book appointments ensuring sufficient information is recorded to retrieve medical and computer record and to identify the purpose of the appointment. To support other healthcare professionals with patient recall, as and when required. Monitor effectiveness of the system and report any problems. Retrieve and re-file records as required ensuring that strict alphabetical order is followed. To scan hospital letters and other patient-related documents into patients computer records, as and when required. General Administration To maintain clinical records. To undertake admin tasks such as reports, management of tasks and other administration work as delegated by the manager. Secure premises at end of day; ensure the building is totally secured for the Albany Practice area. Open up premises at the start of day and make all necessary preparation to receive patients. The post-holders work assignment is determined by the requirements of the Practice, GP Partners, Admin Manager, and the patients needs and will take instructions on a day-to-day basis, from the line manager. To participate in all activities to achieve KPI and QOF targets. Manage the conflicting priorities and prioritise work through discussion with the line manager. To provide holiday and sickness cover for colleagues when required. Each receptionist will be responsible for undertaking specific additional delegated tasks as mutually agreed, or as requested by the line manager or GPS. Equality and Diversity The post holder will support the equality, diversity and rights of patients, carers and colleagues, to include: Acting in a way that recognises the importance of peoples rights, interpreting them in a way that is consistent with Practice procedures and policies, and current legislation. Respecting the privacy, dignity, needs and beliefs of patients, carers and colleagues. Behave in a manner which is welcoming to and of the individual, is non-judgmental and respects their circumstances, feelings priorities and rights. Confidentiality In the course of seeking treatment, patients furnish the Practice with sensitive information in relation to their health and other matters. They do so in confidence and have the right to expect that staff will respect their privacy and act appropriately. In the performance of the duties outlined in this Job Description, the Administration Manager will have access to confidential information relating to patients and their Carers, Practice staff and other healthcare workers. The Administration Manager will also have access to information relating to the Practice as a business organisation. All such information from any source is to be regarded as strictly confidential. Information relating to patients, carers, colleagues, other healthcare workers or the business of the Practice may only be divulged to authorised persons in accordance with the Practice policies and procedures relating to confidentiality and the protection of personal and sensitive data.

title: Receptionist
description: We are a friendly patient centered GP Practice in Raynes Park, and are looking for a receptionist to join our busy GP practice . The ideal candidate will be flexible, friendly, with excellent customer service skills and work well within a team and under pressure, whilst also able to use their own initiative. Good IT skills and an ability to work within a busy environment are also required. Previous NHS receptionist or clerical experience would be advantageous but not necessary as full training will be provided.Main duties of the job. You will be working in a customer facing role, supporting patients to access appropriate services, handling requests for medication, processing documentation and providing administrative support to clinical staff and other members of the practice. We are looking for someone who is flexible, hours and days of the week to be discussed at interview. Starting ASAP

title: Administrator
description: An exciting opportunity has arisen for an organised and motivated Administrator to join the Estates team at North London NHS Foundation Trust. The postholder will work closely with the Associate Director of Capital Development and Estates Strategy, providing day-to-day administrative support. A key part of the role will be supporting the effective management of project files and documentation, ensuring records are accurate, well organised, up to date and easily accessible. The Administrator will maintain SharePoint folders, project records, programme trackers and other key information, helping to ensure appropriate document control and record keeping. The role will also support the Associate Director with diary management, meetings, correspondence, reports, presentations and the monitoring of actions and deadlines. The successful candidate will be highly organised, confident using Microsoft Office and able to manage a varied workload while maintaining a high level of accuracy. This is an excellent opportunity for someone who enjoys working closely with senior management and providing reliable administrative support within a busy Estates and Capital environment. The postholder will demonstrate the Trust's values and The North London Way, contributing to an efficient, professional and well-organised service. The Administrator will work closely with the Associate Director of Capital Development and Estates Strategy, providing high-quality administrative support to ensure the effective organisation and management of the Capital Development and Estates function. Key responsibilities will include: Providing day-to-day administrative support to the Associate Director, including diary management, correspondence, meeting arrangements and monitoring key actions. Managing and maintaining project files and documentation, ensuring information is accurate, up to date, appropriately organised and easily accessible. Maintaining SharePoint folders, programme trackers, project records and other Estates information systems, ensuring effective document control and version management. Preparing and formatting reports, presentations, briefings, meeting papers and other documentation to a high professional standard. Coordinating meetings, including preparing agendas, circulating papers, taking accurate minutes and following up agreed actions. Monitoring actions, deadlines and outstanding information, liaising with relevant colleagues to support timely completion. Communicating professionally with Trust colleagues, contractors, suppliers and other stakeholders on behalf of the Associate Director and wider team. Maintaining accurate and confidential records and ensuring information is handled in accordance with Trust policies, data protection and information governance requirements. Work closely with the Associate Director, providing reliable and responsive administrative support and assisting with the effective management of day-to-day priorities. Manage the Associate Directors diary, arrange meetings and appointments, coordinate meeting requirements and ensure relevant information and documentation are available when required. Maintain SharePoint folders and electronic filing systems, ensuring documents are appropriately named, organised, version-controlled and easily accessible to authorised members of the team. Maintain and update project trackers, programme information, action logs, databases and other Estates records, ensuring information remains accurate and current. Prepare and format correspondence, reports, presentations, briefings, spreadsheets and meeting papers to a professional standard. Provide administrative support for meetings, including preparation and circulation of agendas and papers, taking accurate minutes and maintaining records of decisions and agreed actions. Monitor actions, deadlines and outstanding information arising from meetings and project activities, following up with relevant colleagues as required.

title: Receptionist
company: Partnership of East London Co-operatives (PELC) Ltd
advertiser_name: Partnership of East London Co-operatives (PELC) Ltd
location: Ilford Essex , IG3 8YB, Romford, RM7 0AG, Romford, RM3 0FE, Barking , IG11 9LX
description: PELC is looking for an experienced individual to work as an Urgent Treatment Centre Receptionist, providing excellent patient care service. Your job as a Receptionist will involve working on the front line to support the Urgent Treatment Centre Department. You will be required to provide a professional, confidential, and efficient reception and follow-up service to patients attending the department, as well as deliver clerical support to the clinical areas within the Department. You will also be responsible for overseeing the waiting room. You will need to have experience dealing with the public over the phone and face to face in a professional manner and be able to demonstrate excellent communication skills. It is essential that you are able to work well in a team and have experience of working within the NHS. Where response levels are exceptional we may close the post before the specified date, therefore early application is recommended. If you have not heard within 2 weeks from the closing date, please assume your application has not been successful on this occasion. We recognize the potential of a diverse workforce and welcome applications from all sections of the community. PELC also provides voluntary membership of the NHS Pension Scheme. To provide a professional, confidential and efficient reception and follow-up service to patients attending the department, and clerical support to the clinical areas within the Department.This is a part-time role within a service that operates 24 hours a day, 7 days a week. As such, working hours may vary depending on service needs and staff availability. Flexibility is essential to ensure adequate coverage and continuity of care. The Candidates will be scheduled based on availability and operational requirements. Flexibility and willingness to rotate shifts are essential components of this role. 1. Main Duties & Responsibilities To attend shift on time and take responsibility for the reception from the previous Receptionist and provide a thorough handover to the next Receptionist. This will involve communication any late arrivals, incidents occurred during the shift, specific notes relating to patients, and any outstanding maintenance issues to be reported. To ensure patients are welcomed in a kind and professional manner. Oversee the waiting room To register patient demographics and symptoms accurately and are confidentially recorded on Medway, Symphony, careflow and Adastra software packages. To make use of PELC systems to book in, amend, cancel and arrive patients in line with PELCs procedure, ensuring optimum efficiency of the queue management system. To identify and promote ways of raising the quality of service to patients. Ensuring reception area is kept clean and tidy and falls in line with health and safety at work guidelines. Patiently deal with aggressive, irate and unwell patients in a busy environment and in a professional manner. To ensure information leaflets are restocked and visible including feedback forms, chaperone service, health information leaflets. To ensure all computers are logged in with the appropriate software opened and ready for use. Check emails and fax machine on a daily basis for incoming messages. To ensure the provision of a high standard of clerical support to PELC and A&E clinical and none clinical staff. Dealing with patient queries promptly, efficiently and with empathy. To have an awareness of the layout of the Emergency and Urgent Care Centre, including Majors and Resuscitation, Minor Injuries Unit, Paediatrics and surrounding areas and be prepared to direct patients throughout the department. To be prepared to revert to the manual procedure in place, in the event of a computer down time. To answer telephone enquiries and record messages as where necessary while maintaining a high level of confidentiality at all times in line with the Data Protection Act and the Caldicott Report. To promptly raise clinical incidents to a clinical member of staff on duty. To be aware of PELCs key performance indicators (waiting times) and proactively monitor patient flow at all times and actively communicate with clinicians and escalate to the duty supervisor where necessary. Ensuring all consultation rooms are checked and the appropriate forms are signed as per CQC (Care quality commission) guidelines and ensuring infection control procedures are adhered and to ensure infection control practices are also adhered to in none clinical areas. To follow PELCs Prescription Management guidelines for safe handling, recording and management of FP10 prescriptions. This includes loading prescriptions into printers, filling in indemnity sheets and ensuring their safe handling and storage as per CQC guidelines. Ensuring all PELC GP equipment is checked and is in working order, reporting any broken or missing items to their line manager. Ensuring all signing in/out sheets are updated in real time. To ensure efficient management of PELC medication. This includes managing stock intake, supporting clinicians with dispensing medication and counter sign medication tracking sheets. Accurately recording and monitoring medication room temperatures and reporting any problems to the duty supervisor. To follow prescribed procedure in dealing with any bodily fluid spillages or accidents, reacting quickly and efficiently to ensure infection control standards are met. To provide support to clinical staff as a chaperone when required for the interest of both patient and health care professionals. To complete administrative tasks during less busy times including compiling streaming data from the previous day, cleaning streaming cards, printing forms, amalgamating duplicate patient records and any other clerical duties. Ensuring Special patients notes are read accurately and escalated to the relevant clinician. Ensure that CP-IS database is checked and alerts escalated to the relevant clinician when booking in children. To detect safeguarding concerns and ensure PELC policy is followed in reporting them. Reporting any incidents to the duty supervisor/on call manager. Recording incident on risk/ incident register and reporting this immediately on DATIX. To ensure all statuary and mandatory training is completed in a timely manner, including chaperoning training. To adhere to PELC/Trust working arrangements. This job description is not exhaustive and may be adjusted periodically after review and consultation. You will also be expected to carry out any reasonable duties, which may be requested from time-to-time.

title: Receptionist
description: Job Summary We are seeking a friendly, professional and organised Receptionist to join our GP practice team. The successful candidate will play an important role in providing an efficient and welcoming reception service, acting as the first point of contact for patients, visitors and healthcare professionals. The role involves managing patient enquiries, arranging appointments, supporting the smooth day-to-day running of the practice and undertaking a range of administrative duties. The ideal candidate will have excellent communication and organisational skills, a compassionate and approachable manner, and the ability to work effectively in a busy healthcare environment. A commitment to patient confidentiality, providing high-quality customer service and treating all patients with dignity, respect and sensitivity is essential. Main Duties of the Job Duties will include, but are not limited to: Welcome patients and visitors to the practice in a friendly, professional and courteous manner, ensuring they feel valued and supported. Answer incoming telephone calls promptly, deal with enquiries appropriately and direct calls to the relevant healthcare professionals or departments. Manage patient appointments, including booking, cancelling and rearranging appointments in accordance with practice procedures. Respond to patient enquiries both face-to-face and via telephone or other communication channels, ensuring a helpful and professional service at all times. Process repeat prescription requests received through various channels, following practice policies and procedures. Undertake general administrative duties, including filing, scanning, photocopying, data entry and document preparation. Liaise effectively with GPs, nurses, healthcare professionals and other members of the practice team to support the smooth running of daily operations. Follow practice protocols and procedures, including those relating to patient safety, safeguarding and the management of urgent or emergency situations. Provide administrative support to colleagues and assist with other reasonable duties as required to meet the needs of the practice. The post-holder will be an integral member of the General Practice team, undertaking a range of prescription administration, reception and general administrative duties to support the effective and efficient day-to-day running of the practice. The post-holder will undertake a range of reception and general administrative responsibilities, acting as the first point of contact for patients and visitors. This will include welcoming and assisting patients, managing telephone and face-to-face enquiries, booking and managing appointments, supporting patient registrations and maintaining accurate patient information across electronic and paper-based systems. In addition, the post-holder will act as an important point of contact between patients, members of the clinical team and external organisations, ensuring that messages, information and enquiries are communicated promptly and appropriately. The post-holder will contribute to the smooth running of the practice by providing flexible administrative support to colleagues, maintaining high standards of patient care and service delivery, and working collaboratively to support the wider objectives and strategic priorities of the organisation. Throughout all aspects of the role, the post-holder will be expected to demonstrate a professional, friendly and compassionate approach, maintaining patient confidentiality and ensuring that patients are treated with dignity, respect and sensitivity at all times.

title: Receptionist/Admin
description: Receptionist / Administrator GP Surgery Location: Peckham, South East London Hours: Full Time 40 hours per week We are looking for an enthusiastic and reliable Receptionist/Administrator to join our friendly, busy GP practice in the heart of Peckham. The successful candidates will have experience in a primary care setting, demonstrate excellent interpersonal and organisational skills as well as a level of competency in Information Technology. In this part-time role, no two days are ever the same you'll be helping patients, solving problems, and making a real difference in peoples lives. Work closely with the Reception Team and Practice Manager to deliver excellent reception and administrative services, contributing to patient care and the wider success of the practice. This is a role where you'll be helping people every day, working in a supportive team, and knowing that your contribution truly makes a difference. As a GP Receptionist/Administrator, you will be the first point of contact for patients and play a key role in keeping the practice running smoothly. Your work will be varied, rewarding, and always important. Welcome patients and visitors in person, on the phone, and by email, making sure they feel supported. Book, change, or cancel appointments and help patients with referrals. Guide patients to the right healthcare professional or service. title: Receptionist
description: The GP Receptionist is a key front-line role within an NHS GP practice, acting as the first point of contact for patients, carers, and visitors. The role is essential in ensuring the smooth and efficient running of the practice on a daily basis. You will provide a professional, caring, and confidential reception and administrative service, supporting both patients and the clinical team. This includes managing appointments, handling telephone and face-to-face enquiries, processing prescriptions, and maintaining accurate patient records using clinical systems such as EMIS Web. Working in a busy primary care environment, the role requires excellent communication skills, attention to detail, and the ability to remain calm and organised under pressure. You will play an important part in ensuring patients are directed to the right services and receive timely, appropriate care. Overall, the GP Receptionist role is vital in supporting high-quality patient care and contributing to the effective running of the NHS GP practice. Main duties of the job Provide a professional and welcoming reception service to patients, carers, and visitors Answer telephone calls promptly, deal with enquiries, and signpost patients appropriately Book, cancel, and manage appointments using clinical systems (e.g. EMIS) Process repeat prescription requests in line with practice procedures Maintain accurate and up-to-date patient records, ensuring confidentiality at all times Scan, file, and process incoming/outgoing correspondence and clinical documents Support clinicians with administrative tasks, including referrals and follow-ups Deal with patient related admin duties such as emails, registrations and processing online consultations. Deal with patient queries in a calm and professional manner, including difficult or distressed individuals Ensure compliance with GDPR, NHS policies, and practice procedures Work effectively as part of a team in a busy, fast-paced primary care environment Job responsibilities Patient Services Act as the first point of contact for patients in person and by telephone Deal with patient enquiries in a polite, professional, and sensitive manner Book, cancel, and amend appointments accurately and efficiently Signpost patients to appropriate clinicians or services Assist with recall of patients needing annual or monitoring reviews Administration Duties Maintain accurate and up-to-date patient records using clinical systems Process repeat prescription requests following practice protocols Scan, file, and manage incoming and outgoing correspondence Support administrative tasks including referrals and clinical document processing Processing patient registrations Team Support Work closely with GPs, nurses, and the wider practice team Assist with the organisation of clinics and daily workflows Support colleagues to ensure smooth and efficient service delivery Confidentiality & Compliance Maintain strict confidentiality in line with GDPR and NHS policies Follow all practice procedures, protocols, and safeguarding requirements Ensure a professional and safe reception environment at all times General Responsibilities Manage a busy workload in a fast-paced environment Remain calm and professional when dealing with difficult or distressed patients Work effectively as part of a team and support colleagues when required Participate in training and continuous development relevant to the role
