title: Receptionist
description: Medical Receptionist GP Practice Working days/hours: Monday -14.00pm - 18.30pm Wednesday - 14.00pm - 18.30pm Thursday - 13.00pm - 18.00pm Friday -14.00pm - 18.30pm We are looking for a friendly, organised and enthusiastic Medical Receptionist to join our busy GP Practice team. As the first point of contact for our patients, you will play a vital role in delivering a welcoming, professional and efficient service. Your responsibilities will include managing appointments, handling telephone and face-to-face enquiries, supporting patients with their needs, and carrying out a variety of administrative tasks, including processing clinical correspondence, Docman and eConsult workflows. We are seeking someone with excellent communication skills, a caring and compassionate approach, and the ability to multitask in a fast-paced environment. Why join us? You will become part of a supportive and dedicated team where your contribution is valued, and where you can make a real difference to patients and the local community every day. Provide a friendly, professional and efficient reception service to patients and visitors. Manage patient appointments, registrations and general enquiries, both face-to-face and over the telephone. Identify and appropriately direct urgent patient requests in accordance with Practice procedures. Handle incoming calls, messages and home visit requests, liaising with clinical staff as required. Undertake general administrative duties, including processing clinical tasks, correspondence, Docman and eConsult workflows. Maintain accurate and up-to-date patient records, including data entry, scanning and filing documentation. Process payments for private services and issue receipts where required. Maintain patient confidentiality and comply with Practice policies, data protection and safeguarding requirements. Support the wider Practice team to ensure the smooth running of daily operations and delivery of high-quality patient care. Maintain a clean, tidy and welcoming reception and waiting room environment. Key Responsibilities 1. Reception and Patient Services Provide a welcoming, courteous and efficient reception service to patients and visitors. Respond to patient enquiries in person and over the telephone, providing accurate information and assistance. Book, amend and cancel appointments, including new and follow-up appointments, in accordance with Practice procedures. Use effective communication skills and sound judgement to identify patients requiring urgent attention, ensuring they are directed appropriately without disrupting the smooth running of the Practice. Explain Practice procedures, registration requirements and services to new and temporary patients, ensuring all necessary documentation is completed. 2. Telephone and Communication Answer incoming telephone calls promptly and professionally, directing enquiries to the appropriate person or department. Take accurate messages and ensure they are communicated to the relevant team members in a timely manner. Liaise with the Duty Doctor regarding home visit requests, following Practice protocols. Communicate effectively and sensitively with patients, carers, healthcare professionals and external organisations. Handle confidential and sensitive information with discretion and professionalism. 3. Administrative Duties Undertake a range of general administrative duties to support the efficient operation of the Practice. Process clinical and administrative tasks accurately and within agreed timescales. Manage and action Docman correspondence and workflows, ensuring documents are appropriately processed and allocated. Monitor and process eConsult requests in accordance with Practice procedures, escalating clinical concerns to the appropriate team members. Enter and update patient information accurately on the clinical computer system. Scan and attach incoming correspondence and relevant documentation to the correct patient medical records. Support the clinical and administrative teams with other duties as required. 4. Patient Records and Information Management Maintain accurate, complete and up-to-date patient records in accordance with Practice policies. Retrieve, organise and re-file paper medical records where required, ensuring appropriate filing procedures are followed. Ensure patient records and documentation are maintained in good condition and stored securely. Handle all patient information in accordance with confidentiality requirements, UK GDPR and Practice information governance policies. 5. Payments and Private Services Provide patients with information regarding fees for private and non-NHS services. Accept payments, issue receipts and maintain accurate records of transactions in accordance with Practice procedures. 6. Teamwork and General Responsibilities Work collaboratively with GPs, nurses, administrative colleagues and the wider Practice team to ensure a high standard of patient service. Support colleagues during busy periods and contribute to the effective day-to-day running of the Practice. Follow all Practice policies and procedures, including safeguarding, health and safety, infection prevention and control, and confidentiality. Attend relevant training, staff meetings and development activities as required. The successful candidate will be expected to provide cover for thier colleagues during periods of annual leave and sick leave, subject to operational requirements. Undertake any other reasonable duties appropriate to the role, as directed by the Practice Manager or the Partners.

title: Reception Administrator

This will include but is not limited to the following: To ensure that all visitors, telephone callers, and patients accessing the practice are greeted professionally. To ensure all telephone calls are managed appropriately. To assist patients in accessing the most appropriate healthcare professional to meet their clinical need. To manage the flow of patients and patient administration queries. To ensure the administrative clinical pathways are followed. Reception duties: Greeting and booking in or patients for surgeries and clinics. Dealing with patient enquiries efficiently and courteously. The receiving and recording of telephone messages taking appropriate action Making appointments on Emisweb, by processing appointment requests for today, future appointments from patients in person and on the telephone. Dealing with all telephone queries/requests from patients, and acting as liaison with the Doctors/Nurses as necessary. Pulling and filing medical records as necessary. Processing repeat prescriptions and filing for collection within 48 hours. Taking home visit requests Advising patients of relevant charges for private services Receiving specimens from patients ensuring all their details have been recorded whilst following Health & Safety policy. Administration duties: To have a thorough knowledge of all practice policies and procedures To work in accordance of written protocols Provide administrative support for clinical staff. Filing patient records and correspondence when necessary Opening and distribution or practice post. Registering new patients following the Registration Protocol. Scanning of documents onto the medical system. All scanning should be cleared daily. To send letters to patients as necessary. Photocopying of notes and other information (in reception this includes: ensuring enough forms are printed or photocopied: consent forms, appointment card, change of details etc.). Changing details on Emisweb i.e. Change of address, telephone numbers etc. Cover for other team members may be required for sickness and annual leave. To carry out any other duties agreed between employee and the practice to ensure the smooth running of the practice.

title: Receptionist
description: We are seeking a friendly, organised, reliable and compassionate Receptionist to join our busy NHS GP practice in Southall, serving approximately 5,000 registered patients with a clinical team of 7 GPs. The successful candidate will be the first point of contact for patients, providing a professional, welcoming and efficient reception service. The role involves face-to-face, telephone and online patient enquiries, appointment administration and general administrative duties to support the smooth day-to-day running of the practice. The ideal candidate will have excellent communication and customer service skills, a calm and professional manner, and the ability to work effectively in a busy environment while maintaining patient confidentiality and delivering a high standard of care. 1. Patient Reception and Customer Service Welcome patients and visitors in a friendly, professional and courteous manner. Check patients in for appointments and update their arrival status on the clinical system. Respond to patient enquiries in person, by telephone and through online communication channels. Assist patients with appointment bookings, cancellations and rearrangements in line with practice procedures. Treat all patients with dignity, respect, sensitivity and confidentiality. Communicate effectively with patients from diverse cultural and linguistic backgrounds. Manage difficult or distressed patients calmly and professionally, escalating concerns when necessary. Ensure patients who require additional assistance are supported appropriately. 2. Telephone and Appointment Management Answer incoming telephone calls promptly and professionally. Handle appointment requests in accordance with practice policies and access procedures. Direct calls to the appropriate member of the clinical or administrative team. Take accurate messages and ensure they are passed to the relevant person in a timely manner. Explain practice procedures, appointment arrangements and available services clearly. Recognise when a call may require urgent clinical attention and follow the practice's approved escalation procedures. Never provide clinical advice beyond the receptionist's level of training and authorised responsibilities. Use the practice's clinical computer system, SystmOne, Use the practice's clinical computer system, such as EMIS Web or SystmOne, as applicable. Register patient arrivals and update demographic and contact details in accordance with practice procedures. Maintain accurate electronic records and administrative information. Process incoming and outgoing correspondence as directed. Scan, code or file documents in accordance with practice protocols and staff training. Support the processing of prescription requests, medical records requests and other administrative tasks within the scope of the role. Assist with recalls, patient registrations, appointment lists and other routine administrative work. Ensure all information is recorded accurately and handled securely. Maintain strict patient confidentiality at all times. Comply with UK GDPR, the Data Protection Act 2018, NHS information governance requirements and practice policies. Follow procedures relating to safeguarding children and adults at risk, escalating concerns promptly to the appropriate person. Maintain awareness of confidentiality when speaking on the telephone or at the reception desk. Verify patient identity and follow the practice's procedures before disclosing information. Report any data breaches, confidentiality concerns or incidents to the Practice Manager promptly. Work collaboratively with GPs, nurses, healthcare assistants, managers and other administrative colleagues. Support the daily running of reception, ensuring the reception area remains organised and professional. Assist with incoming post, emails, document handling and general office duties. Follow practice policies, standard operating procedures and health and safety requirements. Attend staff meetings, training sessions and appraisals as required. Assist colleagues during periods of high demand and provide appropriate cover when required. Undertake other reasonable duties consistent with the role and level of responsibility.

title: Senior Administrator

We are looking for someone who is enthusiastic, motivated, a strong team player and willing to contribute positively to our welcoming practice environment. The role involves overseeing patient registration processes, clinical recall programmes, document management, workflow allocation, referral processing, prescription support and the maintenance of accurate patient records using EMIS Web and Docman. The post holder will also support the achievement of Quality and Outcomes Framework (QOF) targets and other contractual requirements through effective patient recall and engagement processes. As a Senior Administrator, you will act as a point of escalation for administrative queries, contribute to service improvement initiatives, support staff development and work collaboratively with clinicians, management and external agencies to ensure safe, efficient and high-quality patient care. Job Responsibilities The post holder will strive to maintain quality and efficiency within the practice and will: Provide day-to-day supervision, guidance and support to the administration team. Oversee patient registration and registration workflow processes. Manage document scanning, coding and workflow allocation using EMIS Web and Docman. Coordinate and monitor patient recall programmes, including: QOF recalls Cytology recalls Immunisation recalls NHS Health Check recalls Learning Disability recalls Diabetes recalls Other long-term condition recalls Support the management of appointment scheduling and patient communications. Process referrals, prescription requests and other clinical administration tasks. Maintain accurate and up-to-date patient records in accordance with information governance requirements. Liaise with external organisations regarding the archiving and retrieval of patient medical records. Monitor administrative performance and identify opportunities to improve efficiency and patient experience. Support the Practice Manager, Deputy Practice Manager and GP partners in achieving operational and service delivery objectives. Assist with staff training, induction and the development of administrative procedures. Support the practice in achieving QOF targets and other contractual requirements. Promote a culture of quality improvement, teamwork and patient-centred care. Alert relevant team members to issues relating to quality, safety and risk. Assess own performance and take responsibility for actions, either independently or under supervision. Contribute to the effectiveness of the team by reflecting on individual and team activities and suggesting improvements. Work effectively with individuals and external agencies to meet patients' needs. Manage own time, workload and resources effectively. Participate in practice meetings and administrative team meetings as required. Participate in audits and quality improvement activities where appropriate.

Direct documents requiring review, action or escalation to the appropriate clinician or Practice team member. Identify documents or information that are unclear, incomplete or outside the post-holders training and seek guidance before processing. Maintain patient confidentiality and follow information governance, data-protection and record-management requirements at all times. Complete the required training and competency assessments before processing and annotating documents independently. Support patient registrations, deductions and updates to patient records. Assist with medical reports, insurance forms, subject access requests and related documentation. Liaise appropriately with hospitals, community services, third-sector providers and other external organisations. Ensure patient information is processed accurately and in line with Practice procedures and data-protection requirements. Assist with appointment-system monitoring and other operational processes where required. Escalate documents, queries or concerns promptly and in accordance with agreed Practice processes. Maintain accurate data entry on clinical and administrative systems. Support performance-related administrative tasks by gathering and recording required information. Assist with updating internal logs, compliance records and monitoring tools, including TeamNet. Follow GDPR, confidentiality, information governance and Practice policies at all times. Provide reception cover when required, ensuring a professional and compassionate service to patients and visitors. Handle queries, signpost appropriately and support patient flow within the Practice. Assist with maintaining Practice policies, procedures and documentation. Support the Practice Management Team with administrative elements of CQC compliance. Contribute to continuous improvement and effective team working. Undertake any other reasonable duties appropriate to the role and required to support the effective running of the Practice. Strong administrative experience, preferably in a busy environment. Excellent organisational and time-management skills. A high level of accuracy and attention to detail. Good IT skills, including Microsoft Office, with the ability and willingness to learn clinical and document-management systems. Ability to follow detailed procedures and apply training consistently. Ability to handle confidential and sensitive information appropriately. Strong written and verbal communication skills. Ability to work independently and as part of a team. Ability to prioritise workload and work effectively under pressure. Willingness to complete training and competency assessments relating to document processing and annotation. Experience in primary care, the NHS or another healthcare setting. Understanding of GP Practice operations and patient pathways. Experience of EMIS or another clinical system. Previous experience of processing clinical correspondence or documents. Knowledge of QOF, IIF and CQC requirements. The Practice Administrator is a core member of the Practice team, providing reliable administrative support and developing the skills required to process and annotate incoming clinical documents accurately. The role requires professionalism, discretion, adaptability and a consistent commitment to accurate record keeping and high-quality administrative support.

title: GP Practice Receptionist
description: We are looking for a Receptionist to join our friendly and supportive Front of House Team, starting as soon as possible. This is a busy, varied and rewarding role. You will be organised, patient focused and confident using IT systems (good IT skills are essential). Experience in a GP surgery would be an advantage but is not essential, as full training will be provided. The role is 20 hours per week, working mornings from 8:00am to 1:00pm on a rota basis Monday - Friday. The successful candidate will also be expected to provide additional cover for colleagues during annual leave and sickness absence, where possible. To use EMIS Web (Now Enlivio) computer system to make appointments for patients in accordance with the current surgery appointment policy. To handle queries both in person and over the telephone according to protocol and signpost according to protocol. In circumstances where a query cannot be answered to make appropriate referral. To ensure, along with other members of the reception team, that the reception area is always manned, and the telephones are answered promptly. Ensure waiting area is kept tidy, and notice board and tabletop leaflet displays are updated regularly. Take requests for visits, ensuring all required information is recorded accurately on and passed to the relevant clinician in a timely manner according to protocol Please see the attached full person spec and job description To use EMIS WEB computer system to make appointments for patients in accordance with the current surgery appointment policy. Work on a rota basis as described Take requests for visits, ensuring all required information is recorded accurately on the patients record and passed to the doctor in a timely manner according to protocol. Take messages for the clinicians and ensure these are put on the system as per the current surgery protocol. Ensure that all communication, appointments and other messages are logged under receptionists own identification details as is practicable. To undertake administrative and other tasks as requested by the Practice Manager and clinicians e.g. helping with audits, call-recall, scanning patient records, opening daily mail and scanning for doctor's review, patient registrations as well as any other requirements To support necessary changes for Plashet Harmony Practice to implement identified system changes. title: Care Navigator/Receptionist
description: We are seeking a highly motivated and forward-thinking Receptionist to join our innovative, training-focused practice serving 20,000 patients in Wallington. Experience is desirable, however full training will be provided for the right candidate. Youll be working within a supportive and friendly team in our modern, purpose-built premises. The GP practice receptionist is responsible for undertaking a wide range of reception duties and providing support to the multidisciplinary team. Duties may include, but are not limited to, greeting and directing patients, effective use of the appointment system, booking appointments, processing of personal information and assisting patients as required To act as a central point of contact for patients, the distribution of information, messages and enquiries for the clinical team, liaising with the multidisciplinary team member and external agencies such as secondary care and community service providers. The successful candidate must be flexible to cover additional hours as required by the needs of the surgery and be happy to work between 7:45 and 18:30 on a rota basis. MAIN DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES To make appointments for patients attending the surgery or on the telephone using the computerized clinical system. To suitably triage and signpost patients to other services where applicable including associated services and external services including community pharmacy To ensure patients who do not have appointments but who need urgent medical attention are responded to appropriately and in line with practice protocols and policies. To cancel and re-arrange appointments when necessary. To support and advise those enquiring about registration or those who need temporary registration To respond to any queries and requests for assistance from patients and visitors To advise patients of relevant charges for private services, take payment, record and issue receipts To appropriately address requests for home visits in line with practice protocols To take pathology samples, and respond to requests for x-rays, certificates, etc as needed To retrieve and file records as required ensuring they are kept in the correct order and filed correctly and safely To make and receive calls to patients and other healthcare professionals as required and directed to do so in a courteous and appropriate manner To divert calls or take messages for others To handle enquiries for online access from existing and new patients and process accordingly To ensure the building is opened and closed correctly in line with internal guidelines and security arrangements Report any premises issues to the building information desk or on site caretaker as required Report any immediate IT, clinical system or other system issues to the relevant provider using the information provided To participate in practice meetings and team meetings To keep the reception and office working areas clear and tidy and suitable for other users at all times To undertake other duties as may from time to time be asked and consistent with the post and where capacity permits OTHER INFORMATION Health & safety: The post-holder will assist in promoting and maintaining their own and others health, safety and security as defined in the practice Health & Safety policy and the practice Infection Control policy. This will include: Using personal security systems within the workplace according to practice guidelines Identifying the risks involved in work activities and undertaking such activities in a way that manages those risks Making effective use of training to update knowledge and skills Using appropriate infection control procedures, maintaining work areas in a tidy and safe way and keeping them free from hazards Actively reporting health and safety hazards and infection hazards immediately when recognised Reporting potential risks identified The practice requires staff to be fully vaccinated in line with current CQC requirements and it also strongly recommends all patient facing staff are fully vaccinated for Covid-19. Data quality: To work within the clinical computer system and other systems to improve data quality. Equality and diversity: To support the equality, diversity and rights of patients, carers and colleagues, to include: Acting in a way that recognizes the importance of peoples rights, interpreting them in a way that is consistent with practice procedures and policies, and current legislation. Respecting the privacy, dignity, needs and beliefs of patients, carers and colleagues. Behaving in a manner that is welcoming to and of the individual, is non-judgmental and respects their circumstances, feelings priorities and rights. Personal/Professional development: To participate in any training programme implemented by the practice as part of this employment, such training to include: To complete all necessary mandatory and other training relevant to the role and as identified and directed. Participation in an annual individual performance review, including taking responsibility for maintaining a record of own personal and/or professional development. Taking responsibility for own development, learning, and performance and demonstrating skills and activities to others. Quality: Alert other team members to issues of quality and risk. Assess own performance and take accountability for own actions, either directly or under supervision. Contribute to the effectiveness of the team by reflecting on own and team activities and making suggestions on ways to improve and enhance the teams performance. Work effectively with individuals in other agencies to meet patients needs. Effectively manage own time, workload and resources. Confidentiality: In the course of seeking treatment, patients entrust us with, or allow us to gather, sensitive information in relation to their health and other matters. They do so in confidence and have the right to expect that staff will respect their privacy and act appropriately. In the performance of the duties outlined in this job description, the post-holder may have access to confidential information relating to patients and their carers, practice staff and other healthcare workers. They may also have access to information relating to the practice as a business organisation. All such information from any source is to be regarded as strictly confidential. Information relating to patients, carers, colleagues, other healthcare workers or the business of the practice may only be divulged to authorised persons in accordance with the practice policies and procedures relating to confidentiality and the protection of personal and sensitive data. DBS: The post-holder will be required complete a satisfactory check from the Disclosure and Barring Service concerning any former criminal convictions. You should note that employment within the practice is not subject to the Rehabilitation of Offenders Act 1974, and that you are required to declare all criminal convictions, even those which are classed as spent.

title: Medical Receptionist
description: MUST HAVE GP EXPERIENCE To act as the first point of contact for patients, visitors, and healthcare professionals contacting Albion Street Group Practice. The post holder will provide a professional, compassionate, and efficient reception and administrative support service, ensuring the smooth operational running of the practice and high standards of patient care. Welcome patients and visitors to the practice warmly, efficiently, and professionally. Answer incoming telephone calls, handling enquiries, scheduling appointments, and routing calls Manage patient requests for repeat prescriptions, test results, and general practice information in accordance with practice protocols. Utilise the practice clinical system EMIS Web to book, reschedule, and cancel appointments for GPs, nurses, and allied healthcare professionals. Manage signposting and care navigation to direct patients to the most suitable service or clinician (e.g., GP, practice nurse, pharmacist, or local community services). Monitor e-consultations and online booking requests, Process incoming and outgoing medical correspondence, scan clinical documents into patient records, and workflow tasks to appropriate team members. Process repeat prescription requests accurately and liaise with local pharmacies when necessary. Register new patients, update demographic details, and process temporary patient registrations. Support doctors and nursing staff with daily administrative tasks Ensure the reception area, waiting room, and desk environments remain tidy, safe, and stocked with relevant patient information leaflets. Assist with opening and securing the practice premises according to standard operating procedures. Participate in staff meetings, training sessions, and annual appraisals. Comply with CQC Policies KEY DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES 1. Reception & Patient Navigation Welcome patients and visitors to the surgery in a warm, empathetic, and professional manner. Direct patients appropriately to clinicians, services, or allied healthcare professionals using practice care navigation guidelines. Respond promptly and efficiently to incoming telephone enquiries, routine requests, and emergencies following practice protocols. Handle patient enquiries regarding test results, repeat prescriptions, and general service pathways with tact and sensitivity. 2. Clinical Systems & Administration (EMIS Web) Use the EMIS Web clinical system to schedule, reschedule, and cancel patient appointments for GPs, nurses, and allied health staff. Process repeat prescription requests accurately and liaise with local community pharmacies as necessary. Register new patients, verify ID documents, and process temporary patient registrations in compliance with NHS guidelines. Monitor online triage requests, digital consultations, and practice messaging channels. 3. Document Management & Workflow Scan, code, and attach incoming clinical correspondence, hospital discharge summaries, and pathology lab results to patient electronic records. Action tasks and messages assigned by GPs, nurses, and administrative management in a timely manner. Maintain strict adherence to NHS Information Governance, GDPR, and patient confidentiality policies at all times. 4. Health, Safety & Practice Operations Maintain a clean, tidy, and welcoming reception and waiting room environment. Assist in opening and securing the practice building in line with daily security procedures. Follow infection prevention and control guidelines, safeguarding procedures (for children and vulnerable adults), and practice health and safety standards. Participate in practice team meetings, annual appraisals, and mandatory NHS training modules.

title: Medical Receptionist
description: The Law Medical Group Practice is seeking a reliable and organised Receptionist to join the team at its Wembley branch. The practice is committed to delivering high quality primary care services to its local community and ensuring smooth day to day patient flow through efficient administrative and reception support. The successful candidate will play a key role in supporting the clinical and non clinical teams by undertaking a range of front of house and administrative duties. This will include managing appointments through EMIS, handling patient queries, processing incoming correspondence and ensuring information is accurately directed to the relevant clinicians in a timely manner. The role will involve full front of house responsibilities, including welcoming and directing patients, responding to queries and providing a professional and efficient service both in person and over the telephone. Working Pattern: Part Time, 27.5 Hours per Week The working hours are Monday to Friday, 1:00 pm to 6:30 pm. Please note: The working days and hours are non negotiable . Applicants must be able to commit to this working pattern. Eligibility: Applicants must be UK citizens and have a minimum of five years of work experience in the UK. The role involves providing comprehensive reception support to the multidisciplinary team within the practice. Key responsibilities include managing patient interactions, handling incoming correspondence, and ensuring accurate distribution of information to clinicians. The position includes front-desk duties such as greeting and directing patients, managing the appointment system using EMIS , booking appointments, responding to patient enquiries, and supporting the smooth and efficient day-to-day operation of the practice. Scan and upload documents onto the EMIS clinical system, ensuring accurate patient record management. Review and appropriately allocate documents within EMIS , forwarding them to the relevant clinician for review and action. Photocopy and prepare documentation as required by clinicians and practice staff. Provide cover for colleagues during periods of absence to ensure continuity of service. Accurately input patient information and updates into EMIS where required. Manage and resolve patient queries efficiently, escalating issues where appropriate. Maintain a clean, organised, and efficient reception environment at all times. Support the clinical team with day-to-day operational tasks as required. Signpost patients to the appropriate healthcare professional or NHS service. Support practice audits and administrative reviews as directed by management. Process incoming electronic communications and documents where required. Scan and attach patient-related documentation accurately to patient records within EMIS . Carry out opening and closing procedures in accordance with the practice rota and operational requirements.

Advise new patients of the registration process. Receive payments from patients and record accurately in cash receipt books and provide receipts Be aware of external organisations and their relationship with the practice e.g. Barnet Federation Hub and choose and book system Keep the reception office, records and waiting rooms tidy and undertake any other tasks which contribute to the smooth and efficient organisation of these areas Attend suitable training sessions or courses, approved by the Practice Manager, in order to enhance skills and knowledge including online training through Blue Stream Academy.

title: GP Receptionist
description: Join Dr Sharma & Rai Practice Group as a full-time GP Receptionist, primarily based at Heathway Medical Centre in Dagenham. You will be a welcoming first point of contact for patients and a valued member of our friendly and supportive practice team. We are looking for someone reliable, organised and confident communicating with people face to face. Previous GP reception experience is an advantage, but not essential. We also welcome applicants with strong customer service experience who enjoy helping people, can manage a variety of tasks and are quick to learn new online systems. Good IT skills, excellent communication and a friendly, professional approach are essential. This is a fixed-term position until 8 August 2027, with the possibility of extension. The role is 37.5 hours per week, working varied shifts between 07:45 and 18:30, Monday to Friday, excluding bank holidays. Pay is £12.71 per hour. Our wider practice group offers opportunities to gain experience, develop new skills and apply for permanent positions as vacancies arise. We reserve the right to close this vacancy early if sufficient applications are received. Early applications are encouraged. As a GP Receptionist, you will play an important role in supporting patients and helping the practice run smoothly. Your daily responsibilities will include: Welcoming patients and visitors, providing friendly and professional assistance. Responding to patient enquiries face to face, by telephone and through online systems. Helping patients access appropriate services, including assisting with online appointment requests. Using our clinical system (EMIS Web) and other digital platforms to manage patient information and administrative tasks. Processing patient requests, including prescriptions, test-related enquiries and general correspondence. Supporting GPs, nurses and other team members with day-to-day administrative duties. Maintaining accurate records and handling confidential information appropriately. Working closely with colleagues to provide a positive experience for patients. Full training and guidance on our practice systems and procedures will be provided. We value teamwork, initiative and a willingness to learn. Job Description GP Receptionist Organisation: Dr Sharma & Rai Practice Group Primary Location: Heathway Medical Centre, Dagenham Contract: Full-time, fixed-term until 8 August 2027, with the possibility of extension Hours: 37.5 hours per week, with varied shifts between 07:45 and 18:30, Monday to Friday, excluding bank holidays. To provide a friendly, professional and efficient reception and administrative service to patients, visitors and healthcare professionals. The GP Receptionist plays an important role in supporting patients to access healthcare services, maintaining accurate records and assisting the wider practice team with daily operations. The successful candidate will be based primarily at Heathway Medical Centre, with occasional cover at other practices within Dr Sharma & Rai Practice Group where required. 1. Patient Reception and Customer Service Welcome patients and visitors in a friendly, helpful and professional manner. Act as a first point of contact for patients attending the practice. Respond to patient enquiries face to face, by telephone and through digital communication systems. Assist patients with appointment requests and provide information about available services. Support patients who may require additional assistance accessing healthcare services. Communicate clearly and sensitively with patients from different backgrounds and with varying needs. Handle patient concerns and difficult situations calmly, professionally and respectfully, referring matters to senior colleagues when appropriate. Maintain a welcoming, organised and professional reception environment. 2. Appointment Management and Patient Access Support patients with accessing appointments and services in accordance with practice procedures. Assist patients in using online consultation and appointment request systems. Provide guidance on accessing the NHS App and other available digital services. Process appointment requests, cancellations and changes as directed by practice procedures. Signpost patients to appropriate services using established practice guidance and care navigation procedures. Escalate urgent concerns or clinical queries to the appropriate healthcare professional without providing clinical advice. Help ensure patients receive clear and accurate information about practice services. 3. Clinical Systems and Digital Administration Use EMIS Web and other practice systems to access and update patient information accurately. Process patient requests received through online platforms and electronic communication systems. Scan, upload and attach relevant documents to patient records. Record patient interactions and administrative activities appropriately. Support the processing of incoming correspondence and electronic documents. Maintain accurate records while following confidentiality and information governance requirements. Learn and confidently use new digital systems as introduced by the practice. 4. General Administrative Duties Process routine patient enquiries relating to prescriptions, test requests, referrals and other practice services in accordance with established procedures. Assist with the collection and distribution of forms, letters and other documents. Support the preparation and processing of administrative correspondence. Liaise with hospitals, pharmacies, community healthcare providers and other external organisations when required. Maintain accurate records and ensure administrative tasks are completed in a timely manner. Support clinical and non-clinical colleagues with general administrative tasks. Assist with maintaining an organised and efficient reception and office environment. 5. Teamwork and Communication Work collaboratively with reception colleagues, GPs, nurses, healthcare assistants and administrative staff. Communicate effectively with colleagues to support the smooth running of the practice. Provide reception cover and assistance to colleagues when required. Share relevant information with appropriate team members to ensure continuity of service. Participate in team meetings, training and development activities. Contribute positively to a respectful, supportive and professional working environment. 6. Confidentiality, Safety and Professional Standards Maintain strict patient confidentiality and comply with data protection and information governance requirements. Follow practice policies and procedures, including safeguarding, health and safety, infection prevention and control, and equality and diversity. Recognise and appropriately escalate safeguarding concerns or situations requiring clinical attention. Treat all patients, visitors and colleagues with dignity, respect and sensitivity. Work within the boundaries of the receptionist role and seek guidance when necessary. Maintain professional standards of conduct and appearance. Previous experience in a GP practice and familiarity with EMIS Web would be advantageous but are not essential. We welcome candidates with experience in customer-facing roles who demonstrate strong communication skills, a positive attitude, good computer skills and a willingness to learn. As part of Dr Sharma & Rai Practice Group, employees may have opportunities to develop additional skills, gain experience across different practice functions and apply for permanent vacancies as they arise. title: Practice Administrator
description: We are looking for an organised, motivated and proactive individual to join The Wapping Group Practice and take the lead in managing our QOF, LES and patient recall systems. This is a temporary maternity cover position, with a fixed-term contract of at least 13 months. Flexible working hours: 25 to 37.5 hours per week . This is an important role within our practice, ensuring patients receive the care they need while helping us achieve our clinical and contractual targets. You will work closely with our clinical, administrative and PCN teams to coordinate recalls, monitor performance, improve processes and ensure accurate clinical coding. We offer a friendly and supportive working environment where you will have the opportunity to take ownership of your work, develop your skills and make a real difference to patient care and practice performance. We will provide the necessary training and support to help you succeed in this role, so you do not need to have experience in every aspect of the job. We are looking for someone who is willing to learn, takes initiative and is committed to delivering high-quality work. The successful candidate will be responsible for overseeing the practice's QOF, LES and patient recall systems, ensuring patients are contacted, booked and followed up appropriately. The role involves monitoring performance against clinical targets, coordinating recall activities with the administrative and PCN teams, managing appointment availability and ensuring accurate clinical coding on EMIS. You will also oversee childhood immunisation and cervical screening recalls, identify areas for improvement and work closely with the clinical team to maximise practice performance. Key Responsibilities QOF, LES and Target Management Manage and coordinate all QOF, LES and other contractual recall activities to ensure the practice achieves maximum performance against targets. Monitor QOF and LES dashboards regularly, identifying areas where performance needs improvement. Take responsibility for managing all targets comprehensively, ensuring patients are recalled, booked and appropriately coded. Regularly update EMIS searches and review performance dashboards to identify outstanding work and missed opportunities. Work closely with the clinical and administrative teams to ensure all targets are achieved within the required deadlines. Patient Recall Management Manage the practice's recall system from start to finish, ensuring eligible patients are identified, contacted, booked and followed up. Generate, distribute and monitor recall lists, ensuring work is completed accurately and on time. Allocate recall lists to PCN recall staff, monitor their progress and follow up on outstanding tasks. Ensure patients who do not respond to initial recall attempts are followed up appropriately. Send validation letters to patients who have not responded after repeated contact attempts, in line with practice protocols. Ensure accurate records are maintained of all recall attempts, patient responses and outcomes. Clinical Appointment Management Review and adjust clinical appointment sessions on EMIS, adding or removing appointment slots where necessary to support QOF and LES recall activities. Ensure sufficient clinical appointments are available for patients requiring reviews, monitoring, vaccinations and other target-related activities. Liaise with clinicians and the management team to plan appointment capacity according to recall demand and outstanding targets. Clinical Coding and Data Quality Ensure all QOF and LES activities are accurately coded on EMIS to support correct reporting and achievement. Identify missing or incorrect clinical codes and liaise with the relevant clinicians to resolve any issues. Provide training and guidance to administrative and recall staff on correct clinical coding procedures. Keep staff updated on changes to QOF, LES and other relevant coding requirements. Carry out regular data quality checks to ensure completed clinical activities are correctly recorded and reflected in performance reports. Childhood Immunisations and Cervical Screening Manage childhood immunisation recalls and targets, ensuring eligible children are identified, contacted and followed up. Monitor childhood immunisation performance and work with the clinical team to improve uptake and achieve contractual targets. Manage cervical screening recalls comprehensively, ensuring eligible patients are invited, booked and appropriately followed up. Monitor cervical screening uptake and identify patients who are overdue or have not responded to invitations. Ensure cervical screening records are accurately maintained, including coding of colposcopy correspondence and relevant clinical outcomes. Ensure cervical screening referral information is correctly recorded and processed through CSMS where required. Work closely with the clinical team to resolve coding discrepancies and ensure screening activity is accurately reflected in EMIS and performance dashboards. Staff Coordination and Training Coordinate the work of PCN recall staff by allocating tasks, setting priorities and monitoring progress. Provide regular feedback and guidance to ensure recall activities are completed efficiently. Train staff on recall procedures, EMIS searches, clinical coding and changes to contractual requirements. Maintain effective communication between clinical, administrative and PCN teams to ensure a coordinated approach to achieving practice targets. Identify areas for improvement and implement changes to strengthen recall processes and overall performance. Performance Monitoring and Reporting Regularly review QOF, LES, childhood immunisation and cervical screening performance. Identify gaps in achievement and take proactive steps to improve performance before contractual deadlines. Provide regular progress updates to the Practice Manager, highlighting outstanding targets, risks and areas requiring additional support. Ensure the practice maximises appropriate contractual achievement and income through effective recall management, accurate coding and timely completion of clinical activities.
